subject: environmental-engineering
intro: Environmental engineering leads to the professions that clean and protect the built environment — designing treatment plants, controlling pollution, remediating contaminated land and adapting infrastructure to climate.

roles.title: Environmental Engineers
roles.what: Research, design, plan and perform engineering duties in the prevention, control and remediation of environmental hazards — waste treatment, site remediation and pollution control technology across water, air and land.
roles.where: Unit 2's treatment process design, unit 4's pollution control devices and unit 5's landfill design and site remediation are the core design work; unit 3's hydrology and hydraulics and unit 6's climate adaptation infrastructure extend the brief.

roles.title: Environmental Engineering Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Apply the theory and principles of environmental engineering to modify, test and operate the equipment used in waste treatment and site remediation — working under the direction of engineering staff and helping develop remediation devices.
roles.where: Unit 2's coagulation, filtration and disinfection processes and unit 4's particulate and gas control devices are the equipment they test and run; unit 5's remediation and unit 1's water chemistry and microbiology back the field work.

roles.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
roles.what: Operate and control the systems of machines that transfer and treat water or wastewater — running plants from control boards, adjusting processes and keeping treated water within standard.
roles.where: Unit 2 is the job description: coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, disinfection and the activated sludge process; unit 1's water chemistry and microbiology explains why each stage works and what the operators must hold constant.

roles.title: Hydrologists
roles.what: Research the distribution, circulation and physical properties of underground and surface waters — studying precipitation, infiltration, groundwater movement and how water returns to the ocean and atmosphere.
roles.where: Unit 3 is the direct match — rainfall-runoff, open channel and pipe flow, and groundwater flow — while unit 5's contaminated-site remediation and unit 6's climate adaptation rely on the water systems hydrologists model.
